subject: FinPay production p95 spike on rwd-m-7q:v2 — request for short mitigation window
messages:
From: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@finpay.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops-team@finpay.com
Date: Fri, 03 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Increased p95 on rwd-m-7q:v2 in production — urgent

Hi Soojin,

We started seeing a sharp jump in p95 latency for the ML-text endpoint backed by rwd-m-7q:v2 at ~08:50 PDT. Our internal dashboard shows a sustained p95 of ~900ms (previously ~210ms) and a small but growing error rate (~0.8%). This is impacting a subset of user flows in payments auth (timeouts on downstream services).

Can Redwood provide an immediate mitigation plan? Ourops team asked whether you can:
- temporarily route traffic to the previous variant (rwd-m-7q:v1) or a lighter fallback,
- reduce batch sizes / concurrency for the endpoint, or
- grant a short SLA carveout while we investigate on our side.

We attached a screenshot of our p95 graph and will provide additional logs if useful. We need something actionable in the next hour to avoid customer-facing errors.

Thanks,
Aisha
Aisha Khan
Head of Platform Ops — FinPay
Attach: finpay-p95-dash-20280803.png

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@finpay.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 03 Aug 2028 09:22:14 -07:00
Subject: Re: Increased p95 on rwd-m-7q:v2 in production — urgent

Thanks for flagging this, Aisha — we see the same signal on our telemetry and are treating it as high priority.

Quick plan we can execute now if you approve:
- Authorize a limited mitigation window (we recommend 4 hours, can extend to 6 if needed) during which Redwood will:
  * Route 25% of production traffic for the affected route to rwd-m-7q:v1 (the known-good variant) as a controlled fallback,
  * Reduce max concurrency from 48 -> 24 for the model pool serving this tenant, and
  * Apply a short-lived search/batch tuning (lowered batch size + KV cache pre-warm) to reduce tail latency.
- We'll monitor p95 and error-rate and roll additional adjustments as needed.
- If the mitigation doesn't improve p95 in 30 minutes, we'll escalate to a full fallback for all traffic and open rollback authorization.

I am looping Marcus and Rachel to confirm the technical steps and Dev for commercial coordination. Laura — would you approve a short mitigation window and confirm any contractual guardrails we should respect (credits, notification to procurement)?

Attaching our internal mitigation playbook for quick reference.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Lead, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
Attach: rwd-mitigation-playbook-v1.pdf

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@finpay.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 03 Aug 2028 09:33:40 -07:00
Subject: RE: Increased p95 on rwd-m-7q:v2 in production — urgent

On Fri, Aug 3, 2028 at 9:22 AM Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Quick plan we can execute now if you approve:

Confirmed — technical details and expected impact below.
Plan (can be applied within 12 minutes):
1) Split routing: 75% -> rwd-m-7q:v2 (current), 25% -> rwd-m-7q:v1 (fallback). This is a realtime route rule; traffic can be adjusted in 5% increments.
2) Reduce batch size from 8 -> 4 and lower concurrency for the affected model pool. This reduces throughput but should cut tail locking that is driving p95.
3) Enable aggressive KV cache warming for the top 100 prefix keys we see in FinPay traffic (warmup takes ~2 minutes).
4) Turn on per-request tracing for the next 30 minutes to capture detailed latencies for root-cause analysis.

Expected outcome: p95 should move from ~900ms -> ~280–400ms within 10–15 minutes after deployment of changes. Error rate expected to fall below 0.2%. If we don't see improvement after 30 minutes we recommend a full traffic fallback (100% -> v1) and a controlled rollback of v2 in the canary lane.

Risks/notes:
- Throughput will drop ~18–25% for the affected route while the split is active — acceptable per FinPay's prior runbook.
- We will create an incident timeline and provide hourly updates; we will not change model weights or binary artifacts during the mitigation window (no risky code changes).

Please reply-all with APPROVE to proceed.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
SRE Lead, Inference Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@finpay.com>, Procurement <procurement@finpay.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Aug 2028 12:05:02 -07:00
Subject: Re: Increased p95 on rwd-m-7q:v2 in production — urgent

APPROVED. Laura authorizes a controlled mitigation window of up to 6 hours for FP-4821 per the plan below. Conditions:
- Limited routing split (25% -> v1) and batch/concurrency reductions as described — Marcus please proceed.
- Notify FinPay procurement and include this mitigation in the incident log; commercial team (Dev) to draft a follow-up note on SLA impact and any credit discussion within 48 hours.
- Post-incident: we require a joint post-mortem within 72 hours and a detailed remediation plan (root cause, fix ETA).

Aisha — we'll aim to stabilize traffic within 30 minutes. Dev, coordinate the customer comms and procurement notification. Marcus/Rachel: keep the timeline and metrics updates hourly to this thread.

— Laura Bennett
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
